# n8n Advanced: Expressions, HTTP Request, and the Code Node

## Overview
This day unlocks n8n's real power and starts bridging you from pure no-code to low-code, which is exactly the growth an automation engineer needs. Expressions are n8n's way of dynamically referencing data - instead of typing a fixed value, you write something like {{ $json.email }} to pull the email from the incoming data, and you can do light transformations inside expressions too (uppercase, math, date formatting). The HTTP Request node is arguably the single most valuable node in any automation tool: it lets you call any API on the internet, even ones with no dedicated integration, by specifying the method, URL, headers, and body yourself - this is where all your Day 3 API knowledge pays off, because you can now connect to literally any service. The Code node is your escape hatch: when built-in nodes cannot do something, you write a small piece of JavaScript (or Python) to transform data, run custom logic, or reshape items exactly how you need. You will also use the IF and Switch nodes for branching (like Zapier Paths / Make routers), and the Set, Merge, and item-editing nodes to build, combine, and clean the data flowing through. The mindset shift here is important: no-code gets you 80% of the way, and a little code gets you the last 20% that separates a hobbyist from an engineer. You do not need to be a programmer, but being comfortable dropping into an HTTP Request or a few lines in a Code node makes you dramatically more capable.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: n8n expressions and referencing previous node data; The HTTP Request node for any API; The Code node (JavaScript/Python); IF and Switch nodes for branching; Merge, Set, and item manipulation. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: In n8n, use the HTTP Request node to call a public API, then use a Code node to transform the response (e.g., extract and rename fields), and reference that data downstream with expressions.
Mini Project: Build an n8n workflow that pulls data from an API with no built-in integration using the HTTP Request node, filters results with an IF node, transforms the kept items in a Code node, and writes them to a sheet or database.
Assignment: Write a short guide explaining when to use a built-in node, when to use the HTTP Request node, and when to reach for the Code node, with one example of each.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.

## Assessment
After finishing the work, open the AI Assessment popup to submit your practical results. DeepSeek will evaluate your submission, calculate a dynamic score based on correctness and depth, and add the points to your CalibiAI profile.
